I concur with the many others who said this would not fit without modification.  I consider myself to be advanced when it comes to building/fixing things and this was a bit of a pain.  Once you do it a few times though, you'll get it down!  Thankfully this product doesn't fit so by the third or fourth time of reassembly you'll be ready to fix all your neighbors' fridges!  The flat spot on the spindle was not long enough on mine, so I used a Dremel with a cutoff wheel to extend the flat spots.  I compared my old one with the new one and it looked "close enough" for me.  But once installed, the auger would not spin freely by hand, and surely would have jammed up the motor if reinstalled that way.  I had to grind about a 1/4" further down to fit properly.

This item is the exact part number replacement for my ice maker, however like several others have stated in their reviews this item is not designed correctly. I was hoping other buyers just received a flawed auger but it appears these just aren't designed properly. The shaft where the blades slide on is 1/8" longer than the original and the tapered part of the shaft does not allow the blade to fit against the plastic washer and leaves approximately 1/4" gap between the blade and washer. The product itself seems durable enough but whoever manufactures this needs to fix the design flaw so that it will actually work as a replacement. I will be returning this and purchasing the OEM Part from a local appliance store.

I read the other reviews about this auger before buying, and a few stated that they had to file or grind down the shaft to extend the flats. I ordered anyway because other sellers seemed to have the same complaint. Got the auger, and sure enough, I had to get out the file and extend the flats about 1/4" further towards the plastic. I'm not sure if this is the "fault" of the seller of this item, it could be that there are different slight variations of this replacement part out there. FWIW, my fridge is a GE Profile PSSS3RGZBSS. I tried to determine the correct replacement part number on the internet, and it was difficult, but I came up with the WR17X11939. This auger is supposed to be a replacement for the WR17X11939, so perhaps the discrepancy in flat extent is due to this replacement not matching this model, or maybe the WR17X11939 is not correct for my GE Profile. Who knows? Anyway, filing is easy if you have a bench vise, and installation is a little fiddly, but all is working now. Part appears to be good quality, I can't comment on durability until a few years have passed. On the original part, the plastic "scoops" at the end broke off. I suppose this could occur if you have older ice that is melted together, and the auger gets overloaded trying to break it up. Hopefully, this new auger is stronger.

This replacement auger did not work for my ice maker. While at first glance it looks identical, the metal spine of the auger shaft was not quite the same as the original.
In the first picture, on the original auger, you can see the spacers riding on the lip of the shaft, with the first blade resting on the spacers.
On the replacement auger, you can see that the shaft was cut too long for the blade to rest against the spacers, creating a space between spacer and blade..
The other picture shows the difference in the length of the part the blades rest upon.

I got my auger today.  When I installed it, I ran into the same problem as Mr. Hoffman who wrote a review on October 20, 2020.  I read other reviews eating a late supper to see if anyone else ran into the same problem.  The flat section of the shaft is not long enough therefore creating a gap between the plastic washers which would cause the auger to not turn properly, and the auger blades could be too tight or  loose.  I had a Dremmel Tool and was able to flatten the shaft a little more so the auger would work.  I would not recommend this auger to people who do not have much of a background in fixing or repairing things.  Also, many people need to know the nut on the end of the auger is a left hand thread which is just the opposite of, "Righty to tight and lefty to loose."  (i.e. you need to loosen clockwise) This is why I gave this review only three stars.
